quests.instruction: Aman put ₹500 into his bank account, which is called a deposit. When he needed money for the school trip, he went back to ___ some.
quests.hint: Which action takes money out of an account?
quests.explanation: To deposit is to put money in. To withdraw is to take it out.
quests.funFact: Piggy banks and bank accounts both help people save money for later.

quests.instruction: At sunrise, the beach was ___ except for two joggers. By noon, it was ___ with families and umbrellas.
quests.hint: Think of how many people are on a beach at dawn and at lunchtime.
quests.explanation: Both blanks need opposites that follow the day: empty at dawn, packed by noon.
quests.funFact: Lifeguards usually watch the busiest beaches during summer afternoons.

quests.instruction: Meera sold lemonade for ₹300 and spent ₹200 on lemons, so she made a profit of ₹100. If she had spent ₹400 on supplies, she would have had a…
quests.hint: Costs bigger than income: think of the lemonade stand.
quests.explanation: A profit is money left after costs. A loss is when costs are bigger than the money coming in.
quests.funFact: A lemonade stand is a classic first business for many young entrepreneurs.

quests.instruction: A country that brings in goods from abroad imports them. A country that sends its own goods overseas…
quests.hint: Which word is the reverse of bringing in?
quests.explanation: To import is to bring goods into a country. To export is to send them out.
quests.funFact: India is one of the world’s biggest exporters of tea and spices.

quests.instruction: Which comment is the opposite of praise: “Excellent work on your project!”?
quests.correctAnswer: “This project needs a lot of fixing.”
options: “This project needs a lot of fixing.”
quests.hint: Look for the comment that points out what’s wrong.
quests.explanation: Praise tells someone what they did well. Criticism points out what needs improving.
quests.funFact: Feedback that names specific things is usually more useful than a general “good job”.

quests.instruction: Palm trees thrive in tropical regions, which are warm all year. The icy regions around the North and South Poles are…
quests.hint: Think of the regions around the North and South Poles.
quests.explanation: Tropical regions lie near the equator and are hot and humid. Polar regions lie near the poles and are freezing.
quests.funFact: The tropics lie between two lines of latitude, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.

quests.instruction: Farmers love the soft, dark soil beside the river because crops grow so well: it’s fertile. A dry, stony patch where nothing grows is…
quests.hint: Which land would you plant seeds in?
quests.explanation: Fertile land is rich and full of life. Barren land is too poor to grow much.
quests.funFact: Rivers often leave behind rich soil when they flood, which is why many farms sit beside them.

quests.instruction: The new puppy was ___ at first, hiding under the sofa. By the end of the week, he was ___, bounding up to everyone.
quests.hint: A puppy hiding under the sofa on day one, and the same puppy a week later.
quests.explanation: Hiding shows he felt nervous. Bounding up to people shows he’d become confident.
quests.funFact: Puppies learn to feel safe in a new home through gentle routines.

quests.instruction: Before riding, she swung her foot into the stirrup to mount the horse. At the end of the ride, she carefully…
quests.hint: Picture someone getting off a horse.
quests.explanation: To mount is to get on a horse or a bike. To dismount is to get off.
quests.funFact: Horse riders traditionally mount from the left side.

quests.instruction: Passengers board the ferry at the dock. When it reaches the island, they…
quests.hint: Which word fits stepping off a boat?
quests.explanation: To board is to get on a boat, plane or train. To disembark is to get off it.
quests.funFact: “Disembark” comes from “embark”, which in turn comes from an old word for a small ship.

quests.instruction: The weather app shows a bright sun for Saturday and a thick cloud for Sunday. Compared with Saturday’s sunny sky, Sunday will be…
quests.hint: The cloud symbol on the app tells you something about the sky.
quests.explanation: Sunny skies show the sun, and cloudy skies hide it behind a layer of cloud.
quests.funFact: Satellites take photographs of clouds from space to help forecasters.

quests.instruction: Mum tied Ria’s shoelaces so tightly they pinched. Ria asked her to make them a little…
quests.hint: Which way should the laces move to stop pinching?
quests.explanation: Tight means fitting too closely, and loose gives you more room.
quests.funFact: Shoelaces can be tied in many kinds of knots, such as the reef knot.

quests.instruction: At the harbor, workers load boxes onto the ship. When it reaches the next port, they…
quests.hint: What happens to the cargo when the ship arrives?
quests.explanation: To load is to put things onto something. To unload is to take them off.
quests.funFact: Container ships can carry thousands of boxes at once.

quests.instruction: The chips in the old, opened packet taste…, but the ones in the new packet are crisp and…
quests.hint: One packet has been open for days.
quests.explanation: Stale food has lost its crispness. Fresh food is newly made or opened.
quests.funFact: Airtight clips and containers keep snacks crisp for longer.

quests.instruction: The cycle race has two stages. Stage 1 climbs for hours, all uphill. Stage 2 is all…, so riders can rest their legs.
quests.hint: Which stage lets gravity do the work?
quests.explanation: Uphill goes up a slope, and downhill goes down it.
quests.funFact: Cyclists can reach very high speeds going downhill.

quests.instruction: A mild cold means a runny nose for a day. A far more serious illness needing hospital treatment is…
quests.hint: How do doctors describe a very serious illness?
quests.explanation: Mild means gentle and not serious. Severe means very serious or extreme.
quests.funFact: Doctors sometimes describe illnesses as mild, moderate or severe.

quests.instruction: A gecko can walk across the ceiling. A cat usually walks on the…
quests.hint: Think of what’s below your feet and what’s above your head.
quests.explanation: The ceiling is the top surface of a room. The floor is the bottom one.
quests.funFact: Geckos have tiny hairs on their feet that let them cling to surfaces.

quests.instruction: In summer, many homes use fans or air conditioners to ___ the rooms. In winter, heaters are used to ___ them.
quests.hint: Which season needs the heater?
quests.explanation: To cool is to make colder. To heat is to make warmer. Seasons call for opposite actions.
quests.funFact: Many buildings have thermostats that switch heaters and coolers on and off automatically.

quests.instruction: The class council voted on a plan for a school garden. Eighteen hands went up to approve it, and three stayed down because they…
quests.hint: What did the three who didn’t vote yes think of the plan?
quests.explanation: To approve is to agree to or support something. To disapprove is to think it’s wrong.
quests.funFact: A majority vote means more than half of the votes.

quests.instruction: Shops often give a lower price per item when you buy in bulk. Buying ten pencils costs more than buying five. Buying two pencils costs…
quests.hint: Compare buying two pencils with buying ten.
quests.explanation: Buying fewer items usually means paying a smaller total, so less.
quests.funFact: A “bulk discount” gives a lower price when you buy large amounts.

quests.instruction: Which of these is almost always eaten cooked, not raw?
quests.hint: Imagine trying to chew it uncooked.
quests.explanation: Raw food hasn’t been cooked. Rice grains are hard until they’ve absorbed water and been heated.
quests.funFact: Rice grains absorb water and swell when they’re cooked.

quests.instruction: The teacher said, “Your handwriting has improved this term.” Which sentence says the opposite?
quests.correctAnswer: “Your handwriting has become worse this term.”
options: “Your handwriting has become worse this term.”
“Your handwriting has stayed the same this term.”
quests.hint: Which sentence says the writing is going downhill?
quests.explanation: Improving means getting better. The opposite is getting worse.
quests.funFact: Handwriting often improves with slow, careful practice.

quests.instruction: A sign says “No bikes allowed.” Which sentence means the opposite?
options: Bikes are welcome only on Sundays.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that takes the ban away.
quests.explanation: A ban forbids something. The opposite is that it’s allowed.
quests.funFact: Many parks have rules about bikes to keep walkers safe.

quests.instruction: Which sentence shows the opposite of “Kabir earned ₹50 for washing the car”?
quests.correctAnswer: Kabir spent ₹50 on a comic book.
options: Kabir spent ₹50 on a comic book.
quests.hint: Look for the sentence with money leaving his hands.
quests.explanation: Earning is getting money. Spending is giving it away.
quests.funFact: Coins and paper money have been used for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Ria held the balloon string tightly. At the end of the party, she opened her hand and…
quests.hint: What happens when you open your fist around a string?
quests.explanation: Holding keeps a grip on something, and releasing opens your hand so it can go.
quests.funFact: Balloons released outdoors can end up as litter, harming wildlife.

quests.instruction: In a group chat, it’s polite to let others finish their thoughts and not to…
quests.hint: Think of someone breaking into another person’s turn.
quests.explanation: To interrupt is to cut someone off. To continue is to carry on without a break.
quests.funFact: Waiting for a pause before replying is considered polite in many cultures.

quests.instruction: The old photograph’s colors have faded. A freshly printed one has ___ colors.
quests.hint: Look at how strong the colors are.
quests.explanation: Faded colors have lost their strength over time. Vivid colors are bright and strong.
quests.funFact: Photographs fade because light and air slowly change the dyes.

quests.instruction: A good conversation needs two skills: speaking clearly and…
quests.hint: What do you do while the other person talks?
quests.explanation: Speaking sends out ideas, and listening takes them in. Good conversations need both.
quests.funFact: Hearing happens on its own, but listening takes effort.

quests.instruction: Chalk drawings on the pavement are temporary because rain washes them away. A mural painted on a wall with weatherproof paint is…
quests.hint: Think of what would still be there next year.
quests.explanation: Temporary means lasting only a short time. Permanent means meant to last.
quests.funFact: Chalk is made of soft limestone.

quests.instruction: Which of these is invisible, even though it’s all around us?
quests.hint: You can feel it blowing, but you can’t see it.
quests.explanation: Invisible things can’t be seen. Air is made of gases that are clear.
quests.funFact: Air is a mixture of gases, mostly nitrogen and oxygen.
